newsitem.title: USA: Compaq off after stock ran up head of Q3.
newsitem.headline: Compaq off after stock ran up head of Q3.

text.p: Shares of Computer Computer Corp fell after its third quarter earnings surpassed the highest published estimates on Wall Street, but analysts said the stock had run up in expectation of a very strong quarter.

Compaq was the second computer maker this week to report good quarterly earnings, but its stock fell on the news. Compaq reported $1.25 a share, while the First Call consensus estimate was $1.07 a share.
"It's obvious and it has been obvious for some time that the market and investors have not believed the consensus estimates," said Eugene Glazer, a Dean Witter analyst.

Shares of Compaq, which had an initial upswing at the opening, were off 1-3/4 to 73, in heavy trading. Shares of Sun Microsystems Inc were off seven to 62-1/2 after Sun's first quarter earnings of $0.63 a share were only two cents better than the First Call consensus of $0.61 a share.

Some analysts said that investors who are not closely following Compaq may also be disappointed with the comments by the company's relatively new chief financial officer, who said he is comfortable with estimates of $1.40 a share for the fourth quarter, typically its more robust quarter.
"He is clearly conservative," said Dean Witter's Glazer.
"Prior to this quarter, we were at $1.40 a share (for the fourth quarter), and our estimates are under review is all I can say," Glazer added.
Analysts pointed out that Compaq's CFO, Earl Mason, said last quarter that he was comfortable with analysts' estimates of $1.03 a share.

"Although we had $1.03, we had heard around that $1.25 was going around on the 'whispered circuit,' as opposed to the 'printed circuit,'" said John Dean, a Salomon Brothers analyst. "It clearly was a surprise compared to the written number, but it wasn't a surprise to the people who had been buying the stock."
